messages.text: Hey Diego, quick intro to what we're building for Link. Basically a campus app that maps student interests onto a concept graph and surfaces connections based on shared rare concepts.
Got it. Sounds interesting, but heads up: since we're dealing with student data, we need to be really careful about FERPA compliance from day one.

Fair point. We're actually running the AI locally on a dedicated box right now specifically to avoid sending personal data to cloud APIs, but I'd love your input on how the department handles this kind of pilot.

That's smart. Local inference is definitely the way to go. Can you send me a rough spec of what data points you're actually storing about each student? I want to make sure it aligns with the university's privacy policy.
Sure, mostly free-text interests and some basic profile info. No sensitive stuff like grades or location. I'll put together a one-page summary for you by the end of the week.
Perfect. Also, let's get the department IT team involved early so we can sort out the authentication and access controls properly before we scale it up.
Agreed. We're using standard session auth for now, but I'm happy to integrate with whatever SSO or identity provider the department prefers.
Great. I'll set up a meeting with IT next week. For now, just keep the scope tight and document your data handling process clearly.
